title: Security by Design: Arteris Expands Its Partnership with Arm - Semiwiki
gist: Arteris is expanding a five-year Arm relationship by deploying Cycuity Radix hardware security assurance across additional next-generation Arm CPU programs, moving information-flow-tracking verification into pre-silicon CPU development. The quiet signal is cross-CPU reuse of security properties, which turns one-off security assessments into a repeatable, scalable assurance process and points to hardware security joining performance and power as a standard axis of processor development.

insights.claim: Arteris has expanded its partnership with Arm to deploy Cycuity Radix hardware security assurance technology across additional next-generation Arm CPU programs, following five years of collaboration and successful use on select Arm CPU designs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A land-and-expand inside Arm's core CPU roadmap converts pilot revenue into program-attached revenue for Arteris — track attach rate across Arm CPU generations.
insights.locator: Arteris has expanded its partnership with Arm

insights.claim: Cycuity Radix is now a larger part of Arm's security assurance process, enabling systematic verification and analysis across critical CPU architectures and performance features rather than a one-time assessment of a single design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Recurring, process-embedded tooling has far stickier economics than project-based security audits; this reprices the Arteris security line as annuity-like.
insights.quote: This isn’t about a one-time assessment of a single design.
insights.locator: Cycuity Radix is now a larger part of Arm’s security assurance process

insights.claim: The security verification is applied before silicon exists, letting potential weaknesses be found and fixed during processor development rather than after tape-out.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shift-left security avoids respin and errata costs; the economic argument that sells the tool is avoided silicon rework, not compliance.
insights.quote: potential weaknesses can be found and fixed before silicon exists
insights.locator: The expansion follows five years of collaboration

themes.theme: Why feature checklists miss hardware vulnerabilities

insights.claim: Modern processor security is more than a checklist of features like secure boot or memory protection, because vulnerabilities also emerge from how microarchitectural state, control logic, debug functions and shared resources interact.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Interaction-level vulnerabilities cannot be closed by adding IP blocks, which is why assurance tooling is a distinct and growing spend category from security IP.
insights.locator: Modern processor security is more than a checklist

insights.claim: Information Flow Tracking matters because a design can perform its intended function correctly while sensitive information still travels along an unexpected path, meaning functional verification passing tells you nothing about leakage.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Creates a verification budget line that functional-coverage tools cannot absorb — a defensible niche against the Big Three EDA suites.
insights.quote: A design can perform its intended function while sensitive information still travels along an unexpected path.
insights.locator: That is the value of Information Flow Tracking

insights.claim: Radix does not simply report that a security rule passed or failed; it provides information-flow overlays, schematic views and waveforms so engineers can trace the route a protected asset took and work backward from an unexpected destination.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Debuggability is the adoption gate for security tools; pass/fail-only competitors will lose designer mindshare regardless of detection claims.
insights.locator: This is where Radix gets interesting

insights.claim: Security requirements are converted into rules that become monitors running inside standard simulators and emulators, so Radix rides existing verification infrastructure instead of requiring a parallel flow.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Low switching friction accelerates adoption and makes emulation capacity a complementary demand driver.
insights.locator: Security requirements are converted into rules

insights.claim: Radix calculates a hardware security coverage metric that shows which objectives have been exercised and where more testing is needed, though the number does not replace engineering judgment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A quantified coverage metric is what makes security auditable by management and regulators — the hook that turns a niche tool into a mandated one.
insights.quote: The coverage number does not replace engineering judgment, but it can help expose what has not been exercised.
insights.locator: Radix also calculates hardware security coverage

insights.claim: Arm's flow begins with architectural and microarchitectural security risk assessments that identify critical assets and evaluate them against known threat models to form security objectives, making threat modeling an upstream input to CPU design rather than a post-hoc review.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Security objectives set at architecture time bind the tool to the earliest, stickiest stage of the design cycle.
insights.locator: Arm applies the Cycuity Radix methodology

insights.claim: The quiet headline is that automation and cross-CPU reuse of Cycuity Radix security properties let assurance work carry forward instead of restarting with every design, which is what keeps verification scalable as Arm expands across programs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Reusable property libraries create compounding switching costs — the strongest moat argument in this announcement and the metric to watch for expansion.
insights.quote: That reuse detail is the quiet headline.
insights.locator: That reuse detail is the quiet headline

insights.claim: The expansion is a signal that hardware security assurance is becoming a standard part of processor development alongside performance and power, implying a new permanent line item in chip development budgets.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If security joins PPA as a mandatory design axis, the addressable market for security verification tools expands from optional to structural across every CPU and SoC program.
insights.quote: hardware security assurance is becoming a standard part of processor development, alongside performance and power
insights.locator: Bottom line: Arm is expanding Cycuity Radix
